name: UX Audit Rubric

levels.0: Fail: the fail sentence describes the page, or the element is missing entirely.
levels.1: Poor: mostly failing; one weak redeeming element.
levels.2: Mixed: about half right; a visitor or crawler would notice the gaps.
levels.3: Good: passes with minor, low-risk gaps.
levels.4: Pass: the pass sentence describes the page with nothing material missing.

scale.na_rule: A criterion marked not applicable is dropped and its weight is shared out across the other criteria in the same category, pro rata.

criteria.name: Primary CTA: clear and on-site
criteria.pass: One visually dominant primary CTA sits in the first viewport, its label names the action, and it keeps the visitor on the site.
criteria.fail: There is no clear primary CTA in the first viewport, or the main CTA sends the visitor to another domain.
criteria.evidence_hint: Hero CTA label + href; note the domain it resolves to.

criteria.name: CTA label matches destination
criteria.pass: Every CTA lands on content that delivers what its label promises (an assessment opens an assessment, 'Learn more about X' opens X).
criteria.fail: Two or more CTAs lead somewhere their label does not promise, such as a contact form, an unrelated anchor or an external tool.
criteria.evidence_hint: Table of CTA label -> destination; quote each mismatch.

criteria.name: Conversion path and booking friction
criteria.pass: A ready buyer can convert on-site in two steps or fewer, e.g. an embedded scheduler or a short form with an instant confirmation.
criteria.fail: There is no on-site way to convert, or the only route is a generic contact form followed by an unstated wait.
criteria.evidence_hint: The form fields, scheduler embed (Calendly/Cal.com iframe) or its absence in the booking section.

criteria.name: Navigation and information architecture
criteria.pass: The main nav has 7 or fewer plainly worded items, each leading to a real destination, and the current location is clear.
criteria.fail: Nav labels are vague or jargon, items are broken or missing, or a visitor cannot find the core offers from the nav.
criteria.evidence_hint: Nav labels and hrefs.

criteria.name: Visual hierarchy and component consistency
criteria.pass: One consistent button system (primary/secondary/text), a clear type scale, and repeated components look and behave the same.
criteria.fail: CTAs come in several unrelated styles, headings compete at equal weight, and similar cards use different layouts.
criteria.evidence_hint: Button class/style variants; heading levels used out of order; screenshots.

criteria.name: Responsive build
criteria.pass: One fluid DOM serves every breakpoint, a viewport meta tag is set, and there is no horizontal scroll at 375px.
criteria.fail: Content is duplicated in the DOM for mobile and desktop, the viewport meta is missing, or the page overflows on a phone.
criteria.evidence_hint: Viewport meta, duplicated heading text, mobile overflow width from the render.

criteria.name: Accessibility basics (WCAG 2.1 A/AA)
criteria.pass: Images have meaningful alt text, html has a lang attribute, a skip link exists, inputs have labels and text contrast looks adequate.
criteria.fail: Images use filenames or stock captions as alt text, form inputs are unlabeled, or content is announced twice to screen readers.
criteria.evidence_hint: Count of images with missing/filename/stock alt; lang attribute; unlabeled inputs.

criteria.name: Indexable page architecture
criteria.pass: Each core service or offer has its own crawlable URL with unique copy, and the nav links to those URLs.
criteria.fail: Core offers live only as #anchor sections of one page, or content is rendered only by JavaScript with no crawlable URL.
criteria.evidence_hint: Nav hrefs (anchor vs page), sitemap URL count, list of service URLs.

criteria.name: Title tag and meta description
criteria.pass: The title (under 60 chars) names the brand and the category keyword, and a unique 120-160 char meta description states the offer.
criteria.fail: The title is missing, generic or just the brand name, or the meta description is missing.
criteria.evidence_hint: Quote <title> and meta description with their lengths.

criteria.name: Heading structure
criteria.pass: Exactly one H1 holds the core keyword theme, and H2/H3s follow in a logical outline with no duplicated headings.
criteria.fail: There is no H1, more than one H1, or headings are duplicated or used for styling rather than structure.
criteria.evidence_hint: H1 list with count; duplicated heading text.

criteria.name: Image alt text
criteria.pass: 90% or more of content images have descriptive, context-specific alt text, and logos carry the brand name.
criteria.fail: Most images have empty alt text, filename alt text (1.png, IMG_123) or stock-library captions.
criteria.evidence_hint: Counts: total / empty / filename-like / stock-like alt; quote the worst examples.

criteria.name: Structured data (schema.org)
criteria.pass: Valid JSON-LD for Organization plus the page-relevant types (Service, FAQPage, Person, Product, Article) is present.
criteria.fail: There is no structured data at all.
criteria.evidence_hint: List of JSON-LD @type values found.

criteria.name: Internal linking
criteria.pass: Pages link to related service, case-study and blog pages with descriptive anchor text, and nothing important is orphaned.
criteria.fail: Internal links are almost all #anchors, or they use non-descriptive text like 'click here' and 'learn more'.
criteria.evidence_hint: Count of internal page links vs anchors; generic anchor texts.

criteria.name: Technical crawl basics
criteria.pass: HTTPS, a self-referencing canonical, robots.txt and an XML sitemap, Open Graph tags, and no noindex on public pages.
criteria.fail: A public page is noindexed, the canonical points elsewhere, or there is no sitemap and no canonical.
criteria.evidence_hint: Canonical, robots meta, robots.txt, sitemap status, og: tags.

criteria.name: Value proposition clarity
criteria.pass: Within 5 seconds the hero says who it is for, what they get and why this provider is different.
criteria.fail: The hero is generic or clever-but-vague, and a visitor cannot say what is sold or to whom.
criteria.evidence_hint: Quote the H1 + subheadline.

criteria.name: Audience and pain articulation
criteria.pass: The copy names the target audience's specific problems in their own language.
criteria.fail: There is no audience or problem framing, and the page only lists features or services.
criteria.evidence_hint: Quote the problem/pain section.

criteria.name: Offer specificity
criteria.pass: Each offer states deliverables, format and who it suits.
criteria.fail: Offers are one-line labels with no deliverables.
criteria.evidence_hint: Quote each service blurb; note any pricing/engagement text or its absence.

criteria.name: Proof depth (case studies)
criteria.pass: At least one case study gives the client context, the intervention and a measurable before/after outcome.
criteria.fail: There are no case studies, only generic claims or one-line testimonials.
criteria.evidence_hint: Case-study links/sections, or their absence.

criteria.name: Content freshness and velocity
criteria.pass: The blog or resources have dated content from the last 90 days, published regularly.
criteria.fail: There is no dated content, or the newest item is over 12 months old.
criteria.evidence_hint: Most recent visible post dates.

criteria.name: Readability and brand voice
criteria.pass: Copy is scannable (short paragraphs, descriptive subheads, plain words) and the voice stays consistent and distinct.
criteria.fail: Walls of text, jargon or buzzword stacks, typos, or placeholder or lorem ipsum copy.
criteria.evidence_hint: Quote an example paragraph; note placeholder text.

criteria.name: Claim substantiation
criteria.pass: Every statistic or performance claim shows its source, sample or method (footnote, link or 'based on N clients').
criteria.fail: Bold numeric claims appear with no source, sample size or method.
criteria.evidence_hint: Quote each stat and whether a source is shown.

criteria.name: Identifiable social proof
criteria.pass: Testimonials carry a full name, title and organisation, and client logos are recognisable and named in alt text or captions.
criteria.fail: Testimonials are anonymous or absent, and logos are unidentifiable (filename alt, no captions).
criteria.evidence_hint: Testimonial attributions; logo alt texts.

criteria.name: Founder and team credibility
criteria.pass: Named people with photos, relevant credentials and verifiable history (LinkedIn, past employers, certifications).
criteria.fail: No named people, or only stock photos and vague 'our team' copy.
criteria.evidence_hint: Names, credentials, photos found.

criteria.name: Maintenance signals
criteria.pass: The copyright year is current, there are no broken links or console errors, and no placeholder or 'coming soon' content.
criteria.fail: Outdated copyright, broken links, visible errors or placeholder sections.
criteria.evidence_hint: Footer copyright text verbatim; console errors; placeholder text.

criteria.name: Contact and legitimacy
criteria.pass: Direct contact details (email or phone, a location), privacy policy and terms are linked, and there are active social profiles beyond one channel.
criteria.fail: Contact is only possible through a form, there is no privacy policy, and no verifiable business identity.
criteria.evidence_hint: mailto/tel links, address, privacy/terms links, social links.

criteria.name: Pricing transparency
criteria.pass: Prices, from-prices or packaged tiers are published.
criteria.fail: No pricing or engagement-model information anywhere.
criteria.evidence_hint: Pricing text or its absence.

note: First draft, before calibration against the Bradbury benchmark. Kept so evals can show the before/after. See docs/benchmark.md.
